back: A program that gives users a friendly interface (forms, queries, reports) to a database.
Form: enter or view one record. Query: a saved request for data. Report: formatted, often printed, output with grouping and totals.
connect, create a cursor, execute, fetchone/fetchall (for SELECT), commit (for changes), close.
User input that is run as SQL because the program joined it into the statement.
An SQL statement with ? placeholders; the values are passed separately, so they are only data.
Parameterised queries (main defence), input validation, limited database rights, no detailed error messages to users.
Saves the changes made by INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE; uncommitted changes are lost when the connection closes.
Requirements, design, build tables, build interface, test, document and train, implement and maintain.
